audit_findings.title: The zero-coupon 2028 notes remain a senior cash claim but are treated only as dilution
audit_findings.magnitude: $575.0 million principal; bridge omission alone equals 18.3% of $3,143.0 million base equity value and $3.90 per current diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash while omitting the note principal, although the zero coupon produces no retained interest expense sufficient to represent repayment; unconditional conversion shares are also included in the denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: The Notes due 2028 will not bear regular interest, and the principal amount of the Notes due 2028 will not accrete.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated claim mismatch. The company expects principal to be paid in cash, and the notes were deeply below their $284.87 conversion price. The omitted principal is large enough to materially reduce every scenario, although correcting conditional dilution would partly offset the per-share reduction.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the bridge with the $575.0 million cash principal claim deducted and include conversion dilution only under scenarios exceeding the applicable conversion threshold; reconcile to the $572.836 million carrying amount and $534.750 million filed fair value.

audit_findings.title: The anchor capitalizes a manufacturing credit that is scheduled to disappear
audit_findings.magnitude: $238.7 million FY2025 AMPTC benefit, equal to 159.6% of the $149.6 million owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The temporary credit reduces cost of revenue and therefore enters the OE anchor, forecast growth, and terminal earnings, despite its statutory phase-down beginning in 2030 and expiration after 2032.
audit_findings.evidence: The AMPTC on microinverters decreases by 25% each year beginning in 2030 and ending after 2032.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated and material: the model grows and perpetuates an anchor containing a temporary benefit larger than the entire anchor. The exact normalized OE impact requires tax-credit and product-level reconstruction, but the filed scale alone can change the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2025 OE with AMPTC shown separately, incorporate the realized transfer discounts and fees, phase qualifying credits down through 2032, remove them from terminal earnings, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may double-count customer prepayments whose performance remains outstanding
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; June 2026 deferred revenue was $582.505 million, contract assets were $169.964 million, and disclosed safe-harbor prepayments or billings totaled $151.4 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash received before performance may be included in the cash bridge while future OE includes the revenue and margin from satisfying the same obligations, without reserving fulfillment costs.
audit_findings.evidence: Contract liabilities are recorded as deferred revenue on the accompanying consolidated balance sheets and include payments received in advance of performance obligations under the contract and are realized when the associated revenue is recognized under the contract.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial outstanding performance obligations but does not identify how much of the balance was collected cash, how much remains available at the valuation date, or the remaining fulfillment cost. Double counting is therefore possible, not demonstrated, and its valuation adjustment cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each June 2026 deferred-revenue balance to collected cash versus uncollected billings, associated contract assets, inventory, and remaining fulfillment costs; add only cash demonstrably excess to those costs and rerun the bridge if material.

audit_findings.title: Long-duration legacy warranty claims may encumber cash outside projected OE
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed June 2026 warranty obligations were $203.206 million, equal to 6.5% of the $3,143.0 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Legacy warranty settlements reduce future cash available to equity; value is overstated only to the extent those payments are absent from forecast OE and are not otherwise reserved in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s warranty obligation provides for the repair or replacement of microinverter and storage products that fail during the product’s warranty term, generally of 10 to 25 years.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and long settlement period are demonstrated, but an omitted valuation cost is not. The supplied record does not show whether OE was built from cash flow that already captures warranty settlements or from earnings containing only current-period accruals. The balance is large enough to investigate, but it is not itself the proper deduction because it is discounted and future OE may already capture payments.
audit_findings.action: Trace warranty accruals, settlements, accretion, estimate changes, and noncash fair-value movements through the OE calculation; project settlement cash flows and deduct only the portion not already represented in forecast OE.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 may be a timing-distorted anchor because of safe-harbor transactions
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified OE effect; $91.2 million of FY2025 revenue was associated with safe-harbor microinverter shipments, equal to 6.2% of $1,472.985 million FY2025 revenue
audit_findings.mechanism: A shipment or revenue-timing shift can distort the latest-actual OE anchor, its working-capital contribution, and every growth and terminal-value path derived from that anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The timing and structure of these safe harbor transactions have resulted in higher variability in our quarterly revenue recognition and overall financial performance.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates increased timing variability but does not establish that FY2025 contained a net pull-forward, nor disclose transaction-specific gross profit, costs, cash collections, or displaced future demand. The impact may be material relative to the $149.6 million anchor, but the record cannot establish its size or direction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain transaction-level FY2025 safe-harbor revenue, gross profit, cash collections, working-capital movements, delivery obligations, and subsequent-period displacement; normalize OE and rerun scenarios if a net timing shift is demonstrated.

audit_findings.title: The denominator includes warrants that had expired before the valuation date
audit_findings.magnitude: at most approximately 2.1 million shares, or 1.4% of the 147.533 million-share denominator; removing that maximum raises base value from $21.30 to approximately $21.61 per share and bull value from $23.87 to approximately $24.21
audit_findings.mechanism: Expired warrants improperly increase fully diluted shares, reducing value per share without affecting OE or aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Subject to the other terms of the 2026 Warrants, the first expiration date applicable to the Warrants is June 1, 2026, and the final expiration date applicable to the 2026 Warrants is July 27, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated temporal error, but its maximum computed effect is about $0.31 per base-case share and $0.34 per bull-case share. Even the full correction leaves all scenario values well below the $36.37 market price and does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Update the share roll-forward through September 6, 2026, remove all expired 2026 warrants, retain any shares actually issued before expiration, and refresh per-share values and the buy-below price.
